title: Kilimanjaro: Africa's Highest Peak
text: Mount Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano in Tanzania, northeastern Africa, and the continent's highest peak at 5,895 meters above sea level. It has three volcanic cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira. Kilimanjaro is one of the world's largest volcanoes and rises about 4,877 meters above the surrounding plains, making it one of the tallest freestanding mountains in the world. The mountain features five distinct vegetation zones from base to summit: cultivated lower slopes, forest, heath and moorland, alpine desert, and glacial zone. Kilimanjaro's glaciers have shrunk dramatically — estimates suggest they may disappear entirely within decades due to climate change.
